author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page below the first as the first page
summary: An owner listing asked for at a page below the first shows the first page as normal instead of the error page. The tolerance covers the unfiltered listing and a last-name search alike.
acceptance_criteria: given an owner listing asked for at a page below the first, when it runs, then the first page of owners is listed and no error page is shown
given a search matching more than one owner asked for at a page below the first, when it runs, then the first page of matches is listed
page zero and a negative page are treated alike, as the first page (Owner records edge case 4)
non_goals: a page beyond the last page — behavior unasked, recorded as an open question
a page value that is not a number — behavior unasked, recorded as an open question
the veterinarian directory's paging — REQ-VET-001 is a separate capability and the owner did not name it
notes: Reported reproduction: opening the owner listing at page zero, or any page below the first, renders the error page. Scope traces to the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1; decisions list is empty, so the requirement is bounded to the request as stated. Page values below the first are the whole of REQ-OWN-005. Both test names are data-driven over the below-first page values.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: No new design ground. The pattern catalog's Web controller row (architecture-principles.md:85) already rules that normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the fix belongs in OwnerController at the same seam that already normalizes the last name (OwnerController.java:98-104, grep-confirmed; the IDE oracle is not connected, so this is the weaker basis). The cause is PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (OwnerController.java:133-137): a page below the first yields a negative index and Spring Data rejects it, which surfaces as the error page. Both acceptance criteria run through the one /owners handler, so a single normalization point serves the unfiltered listing and the last-name search alike. system-design.md needs no new section; the OwnerController Contracts row gains REQ-OWN-005 and names the normalization.
integration_points: Repository boundary: reuse the class-level @MockitoBean OwnerRepository double already configured in OwnerControllerTests setup (OwnerControllerTests.java:70,96). A second, hand-written double inside the same @WebMvcTest class would fork the fixture; the project's mocking policy tolerates the existing Mockito suite, and this slice adds cases to it rather than a new test class.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock in CLAUDE.md's testing strategy, driving the real MVC dispatch and binding for the /owners route.

No new entry point. GET /owners keeps its existing binding: the page value binds to a request-scoped int request parameter, and the Owner form-backing object keeps the data binder's disallowed id and *.id fields (OwnerController.java:60-62).

patterns.description: existing request-parameter normalization at the same handler: a null last name becomes the empty string and a supplied one is stripped, before any repository call

risks.risk: Normalizing in two places, or only inside the paging helper, leaves the view's currentPage model attribute holding the raw below-first value, so the rendered paging links and page indicator disagree with the page actually served.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the handler entry, before both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel read the value, so the query and the model see the same page (architecture-principles.md:85, Web controller row: bind, then delegate).

risks.risk: Widening the fix to a page beyond the last, a non-numeric page, or the veterinarian directory's paging ships behavior the owner did not ask for.
risks.mitigation: Hold to the prd-entry non-goals; both remain open questions in prd.md and REQ-VET-001 is a separate capability.

notes: Five-signal foundational check: none trips. system-design.md is populated and partly confirmed, ADRs record the stack and architecture shape, the vocabulary is written and confirmed, the request-parameter concern has a recorded project-level pattern, and no new bounded context appears. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is silent. The Known Defects table gains no row: it lists behaviors that remain, and this one is being fixed. Vocabulary: prose says Owner and Veterinarian; Vet is the code and page-text short form.

findings.description: theOwnerListingShouldTreatAPageBelowTheFirstAsTheFirstPage captures the Pageable passed to owners.findByLastNameStartingWith and asserts requestedPage.getValue().getPageNumber() isEqualTo FIRST_PAGE_INDEX. This restates an outcome the preceding model().attribute("currentPage", FIRST_PAGE) assertion already covers: OwnerController.addPaginationModel sets model attribute "currentPage" from the same pageToShow value that findPaginatedForOwnersLastName's one-line PageRequest.of(page - FIRST_PAGE, pageSize) turns into the repository's page index (OwnerController.java:127,130-132,141). Once currentPage is asserted to equal FIRST_PAGE, the index passed to the repository is implied by that single line of production code; the captor+verify adds no additional defect coverage and violates the Mocking Policy checklist item "No verify(...) restating an outcome a behavioral assertion already covers" (docs/testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy). The sibling test theOwnerSearchShouldTreatAPageBelowTheFirstAsTheFirstPage does not use a captor and is equally sufficient evidence that the pattern is redundant here.
findings.fix: Delete the ArgumentCaptor field, the verify(...) call, and the trailing assertThat on the captured Pageable; keep the status/view/model assertions, which already witness the normalized page value.
